key_insight: Lost on Campus introduces a benchmark for testing whether vision-language models can reason about space in large-scale, real-world outdoor 3D environments—not just interpret static images or synthetic indoor scenes.
problem_solved: Existing spatial reasoning benchmarks can reward semantic shortcuts rather than genuine spatial understanding, leaving real-world embodied capabilities inadequately evaluated.
method: Introduce Lost on Campus as a benchmark for embodied spatial reasoning.
Evaluate vision-language models in large-scale, real-world outdoor 3D environments.
Shift evaluation beyond static images and synthetic indoor settings; specific tasks and results are not available in the provided, truncated abstract.
impact: The benchmark could help practitioners assess whether vision-language models are ready for real-world embodied applications. It targets spatial understanding that conventional image-based evaluations may fail to measure.
visual_elements: Campus map with an agent viewpoint and route illustrating outdoor spatial reasoning.

paper_title: Lost on Campus: Evaluating Embodied Spatial Reasoning of Vision-Language Models in the Wild
paper_authors: Zehan Zheng, Yanyuan Chen, Deming Li, Yutao Tang, Jianwen Xie
